column2: A New York City subway station platform, standing on the platform edge looking straight down the length of the tracks into the dark tunnel: white glazed subway tile walls with a mosaic name band, blue steel I beam columns in a long row receding into the distance, a silver subway train with its headlights glowing far away in the tunnel, platform benches, overhead fluorescent light, hanging station signs, wet reflections. The platform floor in the foreground is completely empty; the nearest person is fifteen metres away.

The main concourse of a grand Beaux Arts railroad terminal in Midtown Manhattan at golden hour, looking straight across the vast marble floor: enormous arched windows with shafts of sunlight falling diagonally through dust, a vaulted green ceiling painted with gold constellations, a four faced brass clock on a kiosk in the far middle distance, a split flap departure board, crowds of commuters crossing far away. The marble floor in the foreground is completely empty; the nearest person is fifteen metres away.

Inside a small New York corner bodega at night, looking straight down the narrow main aisle to the back: shelves packed to the ceiling with colourful snacks, cans and cereal, glass door drink fridges glowing along one side, a deli counter with a sneeze guard at the back, hanging chip racks, a lottery ticket display, a cat asleep on a shelf, buzzing fluorescent lights, a worn checkerboard linoleum floor. The floor in the foreground is completely empty; the nearest person is twelve metres away.

The squad room of an old New York police precinct at night, seen through a doorway: rows of grey metal desks with green banker lamps, old computers and stacks of case files, a cork board covered in photographs and red string, a holding cell with bars at the back, a wall clock, fluorescent tubes, venetian blinds with the city lights outside, a few detectives far away in the back. The floor in the foreground is completely empty.

The vaulted lower level of a grand Manhattan railroad terminal near the oyster bar: low arched ceilings covered in herringbone Guastavino terracotta tiles glowing warm under lamps, a sweeping ramp leading up to the main concourse, brass chandeliers, a restaurant entrance with red checked tablecloths far away, commuters far away on the ramp. The terrazzo floor in the foreground is completely empty; the nearest person is fifteen metres away.

Looking straight west down the middle of 42nd Street in Manhattan at Manhattanhenge, the setting sun perfectly framed at the far end of the street between the canyon of skyscrapers, golden light pouring down the street and lighting up every facade, long shadows, yellow taxis far away, crowds far away on the sidewalks photographing the sun, traffic lights, steam from a manhole. The asphalt in the foreground is completely empty; the nearest car and person are thirty metres away.

A New York City subway platform with a silver subway train standing in the station with all its doors wide open, seen straight on from the platform: the lit interior of the car visible through the open doors with orange and yellow seats and poles, the car's route sign glowing, white tile station wall behind the train above it. The platform floor in the foreground is completely empty; the nearest person is inside the train.

Looking out through the big plate glass front window of a museum gift shop on Fifth Avenue in New York at blue hour: the avenue outside with yellow taxis, a city bus, the lit facades of grand stone buildings across the street, a stone museum staircase with banners, street lamps coming on, falling autumn leaves. Inside the window a few display shelves of art books and prints on each side, the shop floor in the foreground completely empty.

The view through the window of a moving New York subway car in a dark tunnel: streaks of tunnel lights, cables along the tunnel wall, the lit windows of another train passing on the next track with riders inside, sparks.
